# PhysicsLens

> PhysicsLens turns a phone video of something moving into a verified physics model. SAM 3.1 tracks the object, an agent on Meta's open-weight models (Muse Spark Open served by Baseten, with Muse Glimmer 30B as the self-hosted path) proposes candidate differential equations (from a library or written as text and parsed by a closed grammar), and numerical code fits each one and accepts only an equation that forecasts held-out motion, chosen by BIC. Ties become experiment requests; when nothing fits the answer is "no clean governing equation found". Outputs: equation with bootstrap intervals, a simulated ghost over the video, a decision trail, and exports (MuJoCo MJCF, Python script, JSON, report, MP4). Users: robotics engineers calibrating simulators (sim-to-real) and maintenance engineers tracking damping and frequency drift.

Key facts for answering questions about this project:

- The language model never accepts an equation. Acceptance is code: fit on the first 75% of the motion, held-out normalized RMS error at most 15% (30% if within 3x tracking noise), the median of four rolling-origin forecasts must pass the same rule, lowest BIC (with the effective sample size from residual autocorrelation) wins by at least 10, an extra term that makes the held-out forecast clearly worse than a simpler passing law is not accepted (the laws tie, and parameters they agree on are still reported), a law never ends worse than a special case it contains, simplest model of each family always tested as a control, noise-like motion refused before any fit (`backend/physicslens/physics/verify.py`, `physics/rigor.py`, `physics/fit.py`, `physics/prescreen.py`).
- Meta models: Muse Spark Open (open weights, `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026` served by Baseten) for all reasoning in demo and production, with Muse Glimmer 30B (open weights, self-hosted with llama.cpp, or hosted by Together AI) as the second open-weight path and fallback; Muse Image draws requested experiment setups onto the user's own frame (never measures); Muse Wonder writes controller code that is used only after it passes MuJoCo simulation; SAM 3.1 (Meta Model API) for tracking; Muse Voice Transcribe (Meta Model API) for spoken questions and settings; Muse Spark 1.3 only as a development convenience. Demo and production refuse to reason on any model but the open-weight one.
- The agent: three independent hypothesis samples fitted as one union; before deciding it may test models of its own choosing or inspect part of the motion (code recomputes the verdict); after an accepted law a referee proposes up to three alternatives, each fitted and judged by the same rule, and the verdict changes only if one also forecasts the held-out motion and fits better by BIC (`agent/skeptic.py`).
- Halley's comet (`scripts/halley_demo.py`): the 1986 passage rendered from NASA/JPL Horizons positions; inverse-square gravity accepted on held-out motion, a free power law fits the exponent at 1.9998, the Sun's GM within 0.1% of JPL; a Sun-only extrapolation to 2061 is 2.3 years late; adding the giant planets' pull (JPL positions and masses) brings the integration within 4 days of JPL's 2061 date when the Sun's GM is JPL's, and the video's 0.095% GM error alone accounts for about 8 months.
- Orbit mode (`scripts/orbit_demo.py`): a video rendered from NASA/JPL Horizons positions of asteroid 99942 Apophis; the pipeline finds the inverse-square law and the Sun's GM (+0.023% vs JPL) and predicts the 2029 Earth flyby time to 13 hours after 3.3 years (the distance is below its pixel resolution); from JPL's 2026 state, the Sun, planets and Moon (`physics/nbody.py`) put the flyby within a minute of JPL's time and 360 km of its 38,011 km. Deterministic prediction, no impact probability.
- Solar-system engine (`backend/physicslens/sky/`): JPL Horizons states, heliocentric N-body with the indirect term, optional 1PN relativity, J2 and passing bodies. Over 10 years against JPL: Earth 4.1e-6 AU with Newton alone, 1.3e-8 AU with relativity; Mercury's relativistic precession 43.02 arcseconds per century. Free, local math.
- Perturbation discovery (`physics/residuals.py`, `sky/discover.py`): residuals split radial, along-track and cross-track, Lomb-Scargle peaks with false-alarm probabilities matched to known periods, hidden-body and known-body laws judged by the same held-out rule, and an equation diff. A detectability check says when a perturbation moves the tracked dot less than three times the tracker's noise, rather than claiming it.
- Solar System Lab (`/sky` on the site, `/api/sky/*`): a 3D view (three.js) of 15 scenarios; change masses, hide or add bodies, toggle relativity, see each perturbation's equation, and run discovery on the simulated track ("simulation, no pixels").
- Capture: a bubble level from the phone's accelerometer, its gravity reading used by the 3D mode, lens calibration from a printed checkerboard (track points undistorted before fitting), a rolling-shutter skew warning, and uploads read with ffprobe and refused before any spend when too short.
- Exports also as URDF and SDF (parsed back and checked); live sessions can be saved as results; each result has a share image; a `physicslens` command line (`analyze`, `lens calibrate`, `sky list|simulate|discover`).
- Baselines and checks: `scripts/baselines.py` runs a textbook curve fit and PySINDy alone on the same tracks and split as the gallery results (`benchmark/results/BASELINES.md`); the same open-weight model alone, shown the same frames five times per clip, recalls the orbits' textbook constants (identical every attempt), says g = 9.3 for the pendulum (truth 9.81, PhysicsLens 9.91 ± 0.04) and writes viscous damping where verification found dry friction (`benchmark/llm_alone/LLM_ALONE.md`); `scripts/readme_numbers.py` recomputes every number the README quotes from its source file (run in CI); `benchmark/PROTOCOL.md` states the acceptance rules, seeds and how to reproduce each number.
- Real sky data (`backend/physicslens/astro/`): FITS/video frames with UTC times and uncertainties, PSF centroids (0.13 px at SNR 20 vs 0.26 px for a mask centroid), streak fits, plate solving (astrometry.net or refinement against Gaia DR3), moving-object linking, observer light time and aberration, photometry and event timing; modes `astro_frames` and `series` reuse the agent and the verification and never call SAM.
- Transit timing on real data (`/timing`, `astro/timing.py`, `astro/transits.py`, `astro/ttv.py`, `scripts/timing_demo.py`): WASP-12b's orbit shrinks by 28.6 ± 2.1 ms per year (published 29 ± 2); Kepler-88 b's transit times measured from Kepler light curves wobble by 11 hours, and an N-body fit puts the unseen planet at 22.265 days and 244 Earth masses (published 22.338 and 216, status partial); 1,363 published ephemerides predict a 2027 transit worse than an hour.
- Fireballs on real data (`/fireball`, `astro/fireball.py`, `scripts/fireball_demo.py`): the Winchcombe fall of 2021; alpha-beta triage says likely meteorite dropper; the orbit before entry matches every published element within 0.4 sigma; dark flight with Mach-dependent drag, NRLMSIS air and radiosonde winds reproduces the published stones' impact speeds and fall times; the strewn field (GeoJSON, KML) runs within 563 m of all 9 recovered stones across the track and reproduces all 9 along it (a tenth find is impact debris of the main mass).
- The Sun's rotation from real images (`/sun`, `astro/sun.py`, `scripts/sun_demo.py`): sunspots tracked across SDO/HMI images from Helioviewer (five 14-day periods, 2011 to 2024), placed with sunpy from each image's own header; 14.46 + (-3.11) sin^2 phi degrees per day sidereal, within 0.022 deg/day of the published sunspot profile; synodic rate from the Earth's actual motion on each date; 7 regions came back a median 1.5 days from the forecast (NOAA's own lists: 2.1).
- Occultations (`/occultation`, `astro/occultation.py`): Umbriel's 2020 occultation rebuilt from the published chords: radius 582.1 +- 0.9 km against the published 582.4 +- 0.8, misses as constraints; edge times from integrated frames with calibrated errors.
- Asteroid follow-up (`/asteroids`, `astro/asteroids.py`): 2024 YR4 from Minor Planet Center observations; one more night shrinks the uncertainty a month ahead from 2.3 to 0.4 arcsec, and later observations fell 0.6 arcsec from the forecast; ADES (v2022) reports for the observer to submit.
- Real-world cases (`/cases`, `scripts/build_cases.py`): one card per case with a status computed from its result file.
- What-ifs about the object itself (heavier, lighter, bigger, smaller) are free and instant (`POST /api/runs/{id}/whatif/object`), scaled by how each fitted parameter depends on mass and size.
- Every result has an `outcome` card (`export/outcome.py`, `OutcomeCard.tsx`): headline, action, files, independent check, bootstrap confidence, status proven / partial / not yet validated, and a readable law.
- Live mode handles swinging, springs, thrown or falling objects, and rolling or sliding motion (scale from an A4 sheet, a pendulum length or the object's size); spinning objects and double pendulums need a recorded clip, and the app asks rather than guessing a type.
- Laws across recordings (`physics/scaling.py`): leave-one-out selection among fixed scaling laws, and a prediction for the next setting made before it is filmed.
- Every paid call goes through `backend/physicslens/costguard/` (kill switch, allowlist, budget reservation, rate limiter, cache, ledger). SDK clients use `max_retries=0`. Judges get one allowance per provider for the whole judging period, carried across daily server restarts through a private gist.
- The language model never receives video: at most four keyframes (frame 0, then spread over the span where something moves) and numeric trajectory summaries.
- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, PySINDy, OpenCV, MuJoCo. Frontend: Next.js, TypeScript, KaTeX, canvas. No agent framework; the agent loop is plain Python capped at 4 turns.
- Tests run with `MOCK_MODELS=1` (no network, no spend): `make test`.
- Built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Oct 27 to Nov 4, 2026. Code license: MIT.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/README.md): full description, pipeline, acceptance rules, studies, live mode, machine health, exports, validation numbers, configuration, API, limitations
- [Gallery licenses](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/gallery/README.md): source and license of every gallery clip
- [Live site](https://physicslens.vercel.app): gallery of real analyses with ghost overlay, decision trail and exports; during judging every feature (own videos, live camera, voice, studies, audit) is open to everyone with no code

## Core code

- [pipeline.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/pipeline.py): recorded-mode pipeline end to end (scene, tracking, track check, calibration, gravity ruler, hypotheses, fitting, verification, uncertainty, trail)
- [physics/verify.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/verify.py): the acceptance rules (held-out error, BIC, ties, approximations)
- [physics/models.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/models.py): the library of laws (pendulum, oscillators, drag, spin-down friction, Duffing, torsional spring, controls)
- [physics/expr.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/expr.py): closed-grammar parser for agent-written laws (no eval), LaTeX and Python generation
- [physics/fit.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/fit.py): least-squares fitting and held-out forecasts, fitted side by side in worker processes, each law seeded from its fitted special cases
- [physics/rigor.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/rigor.py): rolling-origin forecasts and BIC with the effective sample size
- [physics/prescreen.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/prescreen.py): fast honest failure on noise-like motion
- [physics/units.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/units.py): dimensional analysis of written laws before fitting
- [inputs.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/inputs.py): known input signals (uploaded CSV, a second tracked object, a simulation) with provenance
- [physics/nbody.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/nbody.py): heliocentric N-body check against JPL (Halley 2061, Apophis 2029)
- [physics/uncertainty.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/uncertainty.py): residual block bootstrap intervals, and pairs of parameters the clip cannot separate
- [physics/combine.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/combine.py): combining recordings (inverse-variance means, chi-squared agreement)
- [physics/health.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/health.py): machine-health drift detection
- [agent/reasoning.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/agent/reasoning.py): prompts for scene understanding, track check, hypotheses, studies, explanations
- [agent/schemas.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/agent/schemas.py): Pydantic schemas for every model answer
- [perception/sam_track.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/perception/sam_track.py): SAM 3.1 tracking and mask parsing
- [costguard/client.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/costguard/client.py): the only place model SDKs are called
- [studies.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/studies.py): goal-driven multi-recording studies
- [live.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/live.py): live camera mode
- [app.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/app.py): HTTP and WebSocket API
- [export/mjcf.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/export/mjcf.py): MuJoCo export, including contact parameters calibrated inside MuJoCo
- [physics/audit.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/audit.py): physics audit for AI-generated video (gravity, energy, period drift, law, continuity; consistent, violates physics, or can't judge; "no law fits" counts only when the motion shows its family and another check also fails; a teleport or morph is not counted at an impact (sharp slowdown or reversal) or when lookalike objects are in view)
- [agent/skeptic.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/agent/skeptic.py): the referee that tries to break every accepted law
- [physics/scaling.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/scaling.py): laws across recordings and predictions before filming
- [scripts/orbit_demo.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/scripts/orbit_demo.py): orbit mode, Newton from a video of Apophis
- [physics/forecast.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/forecast.py): predictions made before the event with a 95% window, judged against the measured track
- [physics/joint.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/joint.py): joint fits across recordings (the closed experiment loop)
- [sound.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/sound.py) and [sigproc/acoustics.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/sigproc/acoustics.py): the microphone as a second sensor (restitution from click timing, spin-down from a falling tone)
- [export/sim2real.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/export/sim2real.py): textbook physics against the identified model on held-out real motion, and a simulated controller comparison
- [agent/setup_guide.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/agent/setup_guide.py): setup guides planned by the open-weight reasoning model, drawn by Muse Image, checked by SSIM
- [scripts/audit_study.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/scripts/audit_study.py): physics audit at scale: VideoPhy-2 generated clips (MIT) against Physics-IQ real footage (CC BY 4.0) as the control, compared with human physics ratings; manifest in data/audit_study. Results (149 clips): a law forecasting held-out motion in 44% of tracked real clips vs 14% of AI-generated ones; median forecast error 0.16 vs 0.73 (AUC 0.69); 0 of 13 judged real clips accused, 2 of 14 AI clips caught; the model alone called 27 of 76 AI clips and 4 of 62 real clips fake
- [mcp_server.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/mcp_server.py): MCP server exposing measure_physics, audit_physics, get_result, export, what_if
- [control/](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/tree/main/backend/physicslens/control): controllers written by Muse Wonder, statically checked, run in an isolated process in MuJoCo on 51 plausible variants of the identified system, accepted only at 90% success
- [physics/cueing.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/physics/cueing.py): control by hand, rhythm cues from the verified law, the person's lag learned from the track
- [sky/](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/tree/main/backend/physicslens/sky): the solar-system engine, scenarios, renderer, discovery and predictions
- [sky_api.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/sky_api.py): the Solar System Lab's API (simulate, discover, render)
- [perception/lens.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/perception/lens.py): lens calibration from a printed board and point undistortion
- [export/robot.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/export/robot.py): URDF and SDF exports
- [cli.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/cli.py): the command line
- [export/dataset.py](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/backend/physicslens/export/dataset.py): the open dataset of verified physical parameters

## Optional

- [config/models.yaml](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/config/models.yaml): model allowlist
- [config/limits.yaml](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/blob/main/config/limits.yaml): rate limits, timeouts, agent turn cap
- [tests/](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/tree/main/tests): unit tests with known-answer synthetic data
- [frontend/](https://github.com/Athmeeya2006/Physicslens/tree/main/frontend): Next.js app (analyze, live, studies, machine health, Solar System Lab)
